overhead-model.step1d: {count} categories on the Categories tab below; {unassigned} accounts unassigned. Group every indirect expense account so nothing is missed.
overhead-model.step2d: The Matrix tab shows each department’s rate from actuals — currently ${rate}/hr composite. A preview only; it never costs jobs directly.

application.title: Ledger application
application.hint: How overhead reaches the books. Report-only keeps it statistical. Net-zero pair posts each project's share to the overhead account WITH the project tag and reverses the same amount without it — job-cost views carry overhead, the account and company P&L net to zero.
application.autoHint: Overhead applies automatically: when hours are approved, each entry's share (hours × the published department rate on the worked day) posts with the same approval — no month-end step, and it never waits for payroll.
application.backfillPrompt: {entries} approved entries (~{hours}h) predate this mode and aren't carrying overhead yet.
application.backfilled: Applied ${total} of overhead across {entries} past entries

lifecycle.title: Rate lifecycle
lifecycle.hint: Who maintains the published rate card the standard method and the net-zero pair read.

modeHints.manual: The engine calculates and recommends; a person reviews the drift below and clicks Publish.
modeHints.scheduled: The worker snapshots the live composite rates into the card at the start of each period.
modeHints.live: Project types read the live engine directly (rate source "live"); the published card is advisory only.

compliance-classes.title: Counterparty classes
compliance-classes.description: What kind of counterparty a vendor is, and what payment control that carries.

compliance-requirements.title: Compliance requirements
compliance-requirements.description: One row per policy: what must be on file, the limits it must show, and what a lapse does.

information-return-box-rules.title: Information return boxes
information-return-box-rules.description: Which 1099/T4A box an account’s spend belongs in. Anything unmapped falls to the vendor’s default box.

income-tax-rates.title: Income Tax Rates
income-tax-rates.description: Enacted income tax rates by jurisdiction, effective-dated — they drive the ASC 740 provision.

fieldHelp.gapless: Gapless means every number in the sequence must be accounted for, with no skipped numbers. Enable it only when your legal or audit requirements require uninterrupted numbering.
fieldHelp.lienWaiverEnforcement: Block means a bill for this class cannot be paid until a signed waiver covers it.
fieldHelp.defaultLienWaiverType: Pre-selected when you create a waiver for one of these counterparties.
fieldHelp.defaultInformationReturn: Used when a vendor of this class does not name a form itself.
fieldHelp.complianceRequirementClass: Leave empty to apply to every tracked counterparty.
fieldHelp.complianceEnforcement: Block payment stops the money; block bill stops the bill being recorded at all.
fieldHelp.requiresExpiry: On for insurance; off for a W-9, which does not expire.
fieldHelp.minCoverageAmount: Certificates below this limit are refused. Limits are never converted between currencies.
fieldHelp.coverageCurrency: Required once a minimum limit is set — a limit is a money amount and must be comparable.
fieldHelp.requiresVerification: Whoever records a certificate can never be the one who verifies it.
fieldHelp.informationReturnBox: Boxes are statutory. What you configure is which of your accounts feeds which box.

informationReturnBox.nec2: NEC 2 — Direct sales of $5,000 or more
informationReturnBox.misc6: MISC 6 — Medical and health care payments
informationReturnBox.misc10: MISC 10 — Gross proceeds paid to an attorney

laborCosting.title: Labor Costing
laborCosting.description: What an hour of labor costs: effective-dated wages, the estimate components applied before payroll actuals arrive, and how standard cost posts to jobs. Overhead is configured separately in the Overhead Model.

rates.title: Wage rates
rates.hint: Company-wide fallbacks resolve by job title, trade, department, subsidiary, then organization default. Employee-specific wage history remains on each employee record.
rates.emptyFiltered: No wage rates match these filters.
rates.annualHoursRequired: Enter annual hours greater than zero
rates.endDateHint: Leave blank to keep this rate open-ended.
rates.invalidEndDate: The end date cannot be before the start date
rates.drawerNewDescription: Add an effective-dated wage fallback for a workforce scope.
rates.drawerEditDescription: Update the effective-dated wage rate for {scope}.
rates.confirmDelete: Delete this rate? Time already costed keeps its snapshot; future approvals will resolve without it.
rates.employeeNote: {covered} of {total} employees resolve to a wage. Per-employee wages and raise history live on each employee's record (Operations → Employees).

components.title: Cost estimate components
components.hint: Added on top of the wage to make pre-payroll job cost realistic (statutory burden, per diem). Replaced by real payroll costs when actuals post — never a permanent layer.
components.name: Name
components.presetCaName: Statutory burden — CPP, EI, WSIB, EHT, vacation (est.)
components.presetUsName: Payroll burden — FICA, FUTA/SUTA, workers comp (est.)
components.workerCompHint: Rate comes from each employee's assigned worker-comp group (Setup → Workforce → Worker Comp Groups; assign on the employee record). The value here is only the fallback % when an employee has no group.

posting.title: Posting
posting.hint: With posting on, approved time posts DR labor WIP (by project) / CR labor clearing at the standard cost rate. Payroll actuals later clear the same account; the residue is your payroll variance.
posting.overheadNote: Overhead is not part of this rate — it is applied by the Overhead Model as its own layer.

reconciliation.title: Payroll reconciliation
reconciliation.hint: Standard labor credits the clearing account at approval; the payroll journal (imported or manual) debits the same account. The residue is your payroll variance — post it out when the period is done.

billing.title: Bill-out rate cards
billing.hint: Effective-dated customer and project labor pricing. Each card keeps its currency, item-level regular/OT/DT rates, general adjustments, negotiated terms, and assignment history.
billing.empty: No bill-out rate cards match these filters.
billing.newDescription: Create the shared book first, then add effective-dated item rates.
billing.createInItemHint: Rate-card creation uses the shared item rate-book workspace so labor, service, and equipment prices stay in one pricing engine. Return here to review labor-specific terms and assignments.
billing.reviseHint: A revision preserves this version and starts a new effective-dated copy.
billing.historicalHint: This is a historical version. Open the latest version to create a revision.
billing.revisionDescription: Base item rates, scopes, and terms are copied. Adjustments below may apply to the whole card or a specific item.

errors.name: Every adjustment needs a name and code.
errors.duplicateCode: Adjustment codes must be unique for each item.
errors.latestOnly: Open the latest version before creating a revision.
errors.afterLatest: The new effective date must be after the latest version.
errors.save: Could not save the rate-card revision.

checklist.wagesDetail: {covered} of {total} employees resolve to a rate
checklist.burdenNone: No components — pre-payroll cost = raw wage
checklist.postingOn: Standard cost posts to jobs at approval
checklist.postingAccounts: Turn on requires WIP + clearing accounts
checklist.trueupNone: Map a variance account to close periods

wizard.title: Set up labor costing
wizard.description: A guided setup for wage fallbacks, payroll burden, and ledger posting.
wizard.q1: How do you want to estimate payroll burden?
wizard.q1Hint: The employer costs your wages cause — taxes, insurance, vacation. An estimate keeps job costs realistic before payroll runs; real payroll replaces it.

burden.canadaHint: CPP, EI, WSIB, EHT, vacation pay. A sensible starting estimate; refine anytime.
burden.usHint: FICA, FUTA/SUTA, workers comp. Typical range is 25–40%.
burden.customHint: You know your number — enter it.
burden.skipHint: Job costs will show raw wages only until you add components.

wizard.q2Hint: Every employee gets their own wage. Search and fill the crew — anyone left blank can use the optional fallback below, and salaried staff can be refined in the workspace afterward.
wizard.orgRate: Default hourly wage (everyone without a specific rate)
wizard.perEmployeeLater: You can add exact per-employee rates in the workspace any time — they beat trade and default rates.
wizard.q3: Post labor cost to your jobs?
wizard.q3Hint: With posting on, approving time writes standard labor cost into the ledger against each project, anticipating payroll.

posting.offHint: Time gets costed for reports; nothing posts to the GL.
posting.post: Yes — post standard cost at approval
posting.postHint: DR labor WIP (by project) / CR labor clearing. Payroll actuals clear the same account later.
posting.variance: Payroll variance account (optional — for the month-end true-up)

wizard.reviewPosting: Standard cost will post to jobs at approval
wizard.reviewNoPosting: Posting stays off — you can enable it later
wizard.reviewNote: Everything here is editable in the workspace afterward — the guide just fills in the same settings.
wizard.nextOverhead: Labor costing covers wages and statutory burden. Your company's OVERHEAD (rent, admin, fleet…) is a separate layer with its own guided setup — classify costs, review computed rates, and apply them to project types.
wizard.fallbackRate: Optional fallback rate for employees without a wage yet
wizard.fallbackHint: Keeps job costing working while records are being filled in — most companies leave this empty.
wizard.wagesOnRecord: Each employee's wage (and raise history) is set on their employee record — exactly where you manage everything else about them. Nothing to fill in here.
wizard.reviewWagesOnRecord: Wages come from each employee's record.

related.overheadHint: The company-cost layer — pools, department rates, and how overhead reaches jobs.
related.rateBooksHint: What you charge — bill-out rates per item and customer, with reg/OT/DT tiers.
related.timeTypesHint: Regular, overtime, double-time — the cost and bill multipliers this page uses.

welcome.title: Let's set up your books
welcome.description: Tell us how your company works and OpenBooks will shape a focused starting workspace around it. You'll review every choice before anything changes.

company.title: Tell us about your business
company.description: These details establish your accounting foundation. Name and legal details remain editable; base currency, industry, and fiscal calendar lock after your first posting.
company.name: Business name

industry.title: What's your industry?
industry.description: We'll recommend a chart of accounts and relevant capabilities for the way your industry works. You review the recommendation before it is applied.
industry.locked: Your industry can't be changed after transactions have been posted, but you can still customize your chart of accounts and features individually.
industry.classificationOnly: Your existing chart and posted history will be preserved. This first-time classification only tunes workspace and feature recommendations.

profile.title: Meet your company where it is
profile.description: OpenBooks can stay beautifully simple today and reveal deeper controls as your team and accounting needs grow.
profile.teamQuestion: How many people will work in OpenBooks?
profile.adapting: OpenBooks uses these concrete working habits—not a vague company-size label—to recommend controls. You will review every enabled capability before anything is applied.

small.title: 2–10 people
small.description: A small team with shared work

essentials.title: Owner-managed
essentials.description: The same trusted person can prepare, review, post, and close the books.

growing.title: Team review
growing.description: People share the work and important transactions should have a clear reviewer.

advanced.title: Formal controls
advanced.description: Duties are separated and approvals, evidence, and close sign-off must be governed.

operations.title: How do you operate?
operations.description: Confirm the work you actually do and the financial structure you operate. Your industry answers are already reflected below.
operations.structureDescription: Answer these directly. OpenBooks never assumes extra legal entities or foreign-currency accounting from headcount or industry.
operations.note: This is a reviewable starting point. Every switch remains authoritative and adjustable under Company Settings → Features, with data-preserving safety checks.

projects.title: Projects & job costing
projects.description: Track jobs with budgets, costing, billing, and profitability.

timeTracking.title: Time tracking
timeTracking.description: Timesheets with submission, approval, and cost/bill rate tracking.

inventory.title: Inventory
inventory.description: Stock tracking, locations, item costing, and assemblies.

subscriptionBilling.title: Subscription billing
subscriptionBilling.description: Plans and subscriptions that auto-generate recurring invoices.

orders.title: Estimates & orders
orders.description: Use estimates, sales orders, and purchase orders before invoices or bills.

crm.title: Sales pipeline
crm.description: Track leads, opportunities, activities, and forecasts before a sale.

multiSubsidiary.title: Multiple entities
multiSubsidiary.description: Run more than one legal entity with consolidation and intercompany.

multiCurrency.title: Multi-currency
multiCurrency.description: Transact in foreign currencies with exchange rates and revaluation.

rhythm.title: Set your accounting rhythm
rhythm.description: Volume changes how much automation helps. Close cadence changes which routines OpenBooks should put in front of you.
rhythm.activityQuestion: Roughly how much activity do you handle each month?
rhythm.activityHint: Count customer and vendor documents, expenses, payments, and bank or card transactions—not journal lines.

light.title: Under 100
light.description: A focused workflow with little automation overhead.

steady.description: Enough activity for imports, rules, and ongoing review to save time.

high.title: More than 1,000
high.description: Automation and continuous monitoring should be ready from the start.

rhythm.closeQuestion: How often do you intend to formally close and report the books?

monthly.title: Every month
monthly.description: Recommended for timely management reporting and early error detection.

quarterly.title: Every quarter
quarterly.description: A lighter formal cycle, with banking still reconciled throughout the quarter.

annual.title: At year-end
annual.description: Minimal formal close cadence; routine reconciliation remains important.

rhythm.note: These are starting preferences, not limits. OpenBooks will never weaken posting integrity or close controls because activity is low.

launch.title: Shape your go-live
launch.description: A few final answers let the readiness guide focus on the work between setup and your first live posting.

fresh.title: Starting fresh
fresh.description: There are no prior balances to bring over; the ledger starts from zero.

migrate.title: Moving existing books
migrate.description: Opening balances, open invoices and bills, and a cutover date need verification.

launch.taxQuestion: Does this company collect sales tax, GST/HST, or VAT?
launch.toolsQuestion: Which of these should be ready from day one?

sample.question: Would you like a company you can explore immediately?
sample.title: Create an industry sample company
sample.description: A realistic company with transactions, projects, reports, and closed periods—matched to the industry you chose.
sample.safety: It is a separate, clearly marked workspace. Sample entries never enter these books, and outbound email, payments, APIs, and integrations are disabled.
sample.error: Your live company was configured, but the optional sample company could not be prepared. You can retry under Import & Export.

review.title: Review your setup
review.description: Here's what we'll configure. Click 'Set up my books' to apply everything.
review.sampleCompanyYes: Create a separate industry sample company
review.note: This creates your accounting foundation and starting workspace. The readiness guide will show anything still needed before your first live posting. Every optional capability remains adjustable from Company Settings → Features.
review.notePreserved: This updates company classification and workspace recommendations without changing the existing chart or posted history. Every optional capability remains adjustable from Company Settings → Features.

applying.title: Setting up your books…
applying.description: Creating your chart of accounts, configuring features, and mapping control accounts.

done.title: Your starting workspace is ready
done.description: Next, the go-live guide will verify the remaining company, tax, numbering, banking, and opening-balance decisions before you post live activity.

general_business.title: General Business
general_business.description: A standard setup that works for any company. No industry-specific assumptions.

construction_contractor.title: Construction & Trade
construction_contractor.description: Contractors, trades, and builders. Job costing, progress billing, retainage, and field tickets.

professional_services.title: Professional Services
professional_services.description: Consultants, agencies, and advisors. Time tracking, project profitability, and retainer billing.

engineering_architecture.title: Engineering & Architecture
engineering_architecture.description: EPC and AEC firms. WBS, phase billing, equipment costing, and progress billing.

it_software_saas.title: Software & SaaS
it_software_saas.description: Subscription billing, ASC 606 revenue recognition, and deferred revenue tracking.

accounting_firm.title: Accounting Practice
accounting_firm.description: Bookkeeping and accounting firms. Multi-client, trust accounting, and engagement tracking.

wholesale_distribution.title: Wholesale & Distribution
wholesale_distribution.description: Distributors and wholesalers. Inventory, landed cost, GRNI, and stock locations.

property_management.title: Property Management
property_management.description: Rental portfolios and property managers. Recurring rent, CAM, security deposits, and fixed assets.

nonprofit.title: Non-Profit
nonprofit.description: Charities and non-profits. Grant tracking, fund accounting, donations, and restricted net assets.

manufacturing.title: Manufacturing
manufacturing.description: Light and discrete manufacturing. BOMs, raw materials, WIP, finished goods, and overhead.

healthcare_practice.title: Healthcare Practice
healthcare_practice.description: Medical and dental practices. Patient AR, medical supplies, and equipment.

empty.title: No flows yet

projects.title: Projects & job costing

timeTracking.title: Time tracking

fieldTickets.title: Field tickets

payroll.title: Payroll

projectScheduling.title: Project Scheduling

inventory.title: Inventory

equipment.title: Equipment & rentals

expenses.title: Expense reports

banking.title: Banking
banking.description: Bank feeds, statement matching, reconciliation, and rules.

fixedAssets.title: Fixed assets
fixedAssets.description: Asset registers, depreciation books, and tax depreciation.

budgets.title: Budgets

continuousClose.description: Always-on close checks in addition to the period close.

advancedClose.title: Advanced close governance
advancedClose.description: Evidence-heavy close blueprints, independent approval routing, controlled locks, and governed close-package publication. Core month-end close remains available when this is off.

apps.title: Apps

propertyManagement.title: Property management

onlinePayments.description: Hosted payment links on invoices (Stripe / Adyen / GoCardless bank debit), surcharge rules, and webhooks that auto-apply receipts to open items.

subcontractorCompliance.title: Subcontractor compliance
subcontractorCompliance.description: Certificates of insurance, lien waivers, and 1099-NEC/MISC and T4A information returns, with payment holds when a subcontractor's coverage lapses.
